items.excerpt: Are perfumes composed? Do they evolve? Polish-Canadian trumpeter and composer Jacques Kuba Séguin says they do, emphatically, with his La Trilogie des Odeurs: Three Works, Three Universes, One Story. In presenting an olfactory world via an auditory work of art, there is a sense that Séguin is taking things well beyond just perfume to an entire world of odors.
items.body:
Are perfumes composed? Do they evolve? Polish-Canadian trumpeter and composer Jacques Kuba Séguin says they do, emphatically, with his La Trilogie des Odeurs: Three Works, Three Universes, One Story.

In presenting an olfactory world via an auditory work of art, there is a sense that Séguin is taking things well beyond just perfume to an entire world of odors. It also suggests an entanglement of the senses, and Séguin pushes this suggestion to the max with this trilogy in three separate albums. For Parfum no. 1, he convenes a jazz quartet with pianist Jean-Michel Pilc, bassist Rémi-Jean Leblanc, drummer Kevin Warren, with vocalist Elizabeth Shepherd sitting in on one tune. Leave the connection of odor to sound to the listener here. Synesthesia—where the stimulation of one sense triggers experiences in another—is a real thing. Pianist Jessica Williams said she saw colors with every note or chord she played.

Of the three Parfum albums, No. 1, 2 and 3, Parfum no. 1 is the starkest—a spare, dry sound that may evoke the smell of desert sage as it rides the Santa Ana winds through the chaparral, picking up molecules of the menthol eucalyptus that flourishes in the riverbeds, the rich aromas of damp earth from which these craggy apparitions writhe.

There is much space here, like that desert landscape that birthed the sage. Melodic simplicity and repetition make the music sound ritualistic in a beautiful way. Elizabeth Shepherd's vocals (invocations?) in French are hushed whisperings on "Je suis là."

The music is expressed with an understated patience, as it was in Miles Davis' Ascenseur pour l'échafaud (Fontana, 1957). It is an inward sound that invites reflection and contemplation.

The three albums as a whole are described as a trilogy of smells celebrating the olfactory memories of our lives. This, in itself, marks out ambitious territory via three distinct albums—Parfum no. 1 utilizing the jazz quartet; Parfum no 2 employing a 17-piece jazz band; and Parfum no. 3 bringing in a symphony orchestra, taking the ambitious aspect off the charts.

The olfactory experiences described, auditorily, on Parfum no. 1 are subtle, whiffs of mixed fragrances. Parfum no. 2, the big band set, brings in a riot of bright smells, with brassy primary colors underlain by understated pastel scents and rainbow swirls of harmonic whirlpoolings.

The final chapter, Parfum no. 3 enfolds the jazz quartet with L'Orchestre Symphonique de Trois-Rivières, led by Alain Trudel. Séguin speaks of: "Base notes, or earth notes...the essence of the perfume, the part that clings to the skin and remains imprinted in objects as well as in the soul." While the first chapter of this trilogy speaks to a simplicity of expression and the elementary, youthful experience of the fragrance, Parfum no. 3 takes that early introduction into the complexities of understanding born of time and wisdom into a richer and more complex landscape.

Track Listing: CD 1: La danse du hasard; Promesse de souvenirs; Rencontre au berceau; Je suis là; Éphémère; Candeur. CD 2: La danse du hasard et des dangers; 26 printemps; Paysage pour Muniak; 40 is the new 30; Gratitude. CD 3: How we start again; Il n'y a pas de hasard; Fugue avec Anaïs (à Métis); Entre l'exil et l'insomnie - partie I L'exil; In coelum; Entre l'exil et l'insomnie - partie II L'insomnie; le cortège des fragrances - Les aléas de Mme P.

Personnel: Jacques Kuba Seguin (trumpet), Jean-Michel Pilc (piano), Rémi-Jean Leblanc (bass), Kevin Warren (drums). Additional: Elizabeth Shepherd (vocals). CD 2: L'orchestre de Nationale de Jazz de Montreal. CD 3: Orchestre des Trois Rivieres.

Title: La Trilogie des Odeurs | Year Released: 2026 | Record Label: Odd Sound Records

items.excerpt: Rightfully described as a thinking (wo)man's jazz musician, trumpeter-composer-bandleader Steven Bernstein makes deeply cerebral music no matter whether with his own ensembles such as Sexmob and Millennial Territory Orchestra or in heady collaborations with other artists such Jacob Fred Jazz Odyssey.
items.body:
Rightfully described as a thinking (wo)man's jazz musician, trumpeter-composer-bandleader Steven Bernstein makes deeply cerebral music no matter whether with his own ensembles such as Sexmob and Millennial Territory Orchestra or in heady collaborations with other artists such Jacob Fred Jazz Odyssey (see Race Riot Suite (Royal Potato Family, 2011)).

In fact, the products of his imagination resound with such visceral force that those creations render an impact comparable to his membership in Levon Helm's Midnight Ramble Band (or MTO's tribute to Sly Stone). ResoNation Trio and Ultra Resonance, are similarly charged, the former a forward-thinking yet traditionalist-leaning project for which Bernstein recruited the estimable rhythm section of bassist Scott Colley and drummer Nasheet Waits, the latter is a reimagining of that threesome's music overseen by pedigreed engineer and producer Scotty Hard (a long-time collaborator of visionaries unto themselves, Medeski Martin & Wood).

The former is as skeletal as the latter is dense. Yet the two recordings, distinctly different in concept and execution, are nevertheless inextricably linked. Each, in its own way, is a thought-provoking piece, with the respective virtues redolent when played separately or together in sequence, either in the configuration of the single CD or the double vinyl package.

The abstract likes of Bernstein-Colley-Waits' "Turf" benefit as much from the space in the arrangement as the linear progression the three pursue in "Pettiford." Meanwhile, corresponding titles of the companion piece, such as "Rubidium," function similarly, gateways into more or less otherworldly realms.

It is not necessary to listen to Ultra Resonance on headphones to appreciate its aura. Still, that method can reveal more of the multiple layers in the recordings. And, in its own way, that method also proves to be comparatively applicable to the acoustic music: the patient and probing human three-way human interactions that comprise "Woodstock," for instance, radiate both the physical and mental effort involved in the musicianship.

Hard's deeply insistent reformulation of the music through the use of keyboards, various other instruments and percussion, in combination with Jeremy Gustin's varied rhythm devices, emits a presence as haunting as that in the spacious interplay of the ResoNation Trio. Selections from the latter like the one non-original, the blues of "Sitting On Top of the World," resound with comparable levels of mental acumen infused with technical expertise.

A comparatively spooky atmosphere thus pervades most of this seventy-six minutes, even as it is presented in cuts of mostly 3 to 5 minute duration. With its infectious lively cheer, the penultimate track by the trumpeter, bassist and drummer, titled "South," may be the exception to the rule.

Accordingly, the sounds from the three-man ensemble flicker in and out of the well-defined, but dark audio mix during "Argon." And, without ever going on too long to become monotonous, there are just enough similar turns of melody to render more pronounced the heavily rhythmic likes of "Titano." In the end, the overall pacing is that of a well-sequenced live set, without an overabundance of aural esoterica.

It is thus indicative of the seamless yet malleable nature of ResoNation Trio and Ultra Resonance that various elements from each can be interwoven with the other. Reprogramming the CD tracks or alternating the four sides of vinyl extends both the accessibility and the durability of Steven Bernstein and company's eccentric musical orthodoxy.

Track Listing: Turf; Pettiford; Two Shakes; Woodstock; August 3; West; Mammoth; Question; South; Sitting on Top of the World; Argon; Erbium; Chromium; Vibranium; Rubidium; Titano; Radon; Niobium.

Personnel: Steven Bernstein (trumpet, G-trumpet, flugelhorn, EVI), Scott Colley (bass), Nasheet Waits (drums), Scotty Hard (organ, Hammond B3, electronics, percussion), Jeremy Gustin (drums, percussion).

Title: ResoNation Trio/Ultra Resonance | Year Released: 2026 | Record Label: Royal Potato Family

items.excerpt: Larry McCray's Heartbreak City, released on Keeping the Blues Alive Records, is steeped in grit, anguish, resilience and hard-won joy. The album reflects the life of a working-class blues man who sharpened his craft in the clubs of Saginaw after shifts on the General Motors assembly line, before touring nationally and eventually across Europe with Albert Collins.
items.body:
Larry McCray's Heartbreak City, released on Keeping the Blues Alive Records, is steeped in grit, anguish, resilience and hard-won joy. The album reflects the life of a working-class blues man who sharpened his craft in the clubs of Saginaw after shifts on the General Motors assembly line, before touring nationally and eventually across Europe with Albert Collins. Every track carries the emotional weight of decades spent earning success the hard way, drawing deeply from McCray's Arkansas roots while sounding fully grounded in the modern blues tradition.

"Try to Be a Good Man," co-written by McCray, serves as both introduction and mission statement. Riding a chugging roadhouse groove—with a bright, punctuating all-star horn section featuring Dan Fornero, Wayne Bergeron, Andy Martin and Sal Lozano—the song doubles as advice for younger men navigating relationships. McCray's baritone, earthy, warm and unforced, anchors lines such as: "Give her all the love you can and do your best to understand." His guitar work is concise and expressive, delivering sharp, brittle, conversational bends that echo the influence of Little Milton without slipping into imitation.

The title track provides the album's emotional center. Built on a deep blues-rock pocket shaped by the modern production style associated with producers Joe Bonamassa and Josh Smith, "Heartbreak City" unfolds with the restless momentum of an open highway. McCray's stinging guitar lines recall Albert King, while his vocal phrasing again nods to Milton. The song captures the album's defining theme: a man worn down by loss, disappointment and the daily grind, yet still unwilling to surrender. It is weary and determined at the same time, balancing vulnerability with quiet resolve.

On "Everything Falls on Me," McCray channels his frustration through a mid-tempo blues-rock groove shaped by Bo Diddley-style syncopation and terse, declarative guitar figures reminiscent of Chuck Berry. Its lyrics about carrying everyone else's burdens strike a familiar chord without lapsing into self-pity. "When it comes to disaster, Red Cross got nothin' on me / I've cleaned up more messes than the human eye can see / Be it friend or family or someone I just met / They only hit me up for something, anything they can get."

McCray's songwriting strengths surface again in "Bye Bye Blues," co-written with Charlie Walmsley and nominated for Song of the Year at the 2026 Blues Music Awards. Built around the line, "When I said hello to you, I said goodbye to the blues," the song balances classic blues sentiment with understated optimism and demonstrates McCray's ability to write memorable, emotionally direct material.

Throughout Heartbreak City, McCray honors the artists who shaped him while remaining unmistakably himself. Positioned somewhere between Albert King's fire and Little Milton's silky soulfulness, he delivers performances defined by warmth, grit and emotional clarity. In an era still searching for towering modern blues voices, McCray makes a compelling case for his place near the top of the genre's current generation.

Track Listing: Try To Be A Good Man; Heartbreak City; Bye Bye Blues; Bright Side; Everything Falls On Me; I Know What I Have Done; Keep On Loving My Baby; Hangman; Stop Your Crying; Crazy World.

Personnel: Larry McCray (guitar, electric), Joe Bonamassa (guitar), Josh Smith (guitar), Reese Wynans (keyboards), Calvin Turner (bass), Lemar Carter (drums), Kirk Fletcher (guitar), Jade Macrae (vocals), Dannielle De Andrea (vocals), Dan Fornero (trumpet/flugelhorn), Wayne Bergeron (trumpet/flugelhorn), Andy Martin (trombone/bass trombone), Sal Lozano (saxophone/baritone saxophone/flutes).

Title: Heartbreak City | Year Released: 2025 | Record Label: Keeping the Blues Alive Records

items.excerpt: Evidence lives up to its title very well. A lot of music in this fairly short album that makes itself heard with surprising simplicity. EVIDENCE is a quartet: reeds, trombone, cello and drums. An unusual formation, but one that recalls Henry Threadgill's Zooid from 2015 onwards.
items.body:
Evidence lives up to its title very well. A lot of music in this fairly short album that makes itself heard with surprising simplicity.

EVIDENCE is a quartet: reeds, trombone, cello and drums. An unusual formation, but one that recalls Henry Threadgill's Zooid from 2015 onwards (without the guitar): In For A Penny, In For A Pound (Pi Recordings, 2015) and Poof. Sol Léna-Schroll (alto saxophone and clarinet) is Threadgill, Jørgen Bjelkerud (trombone) is Jose Davila, Joel Ring that of Christopher Hoffman, and Trym Saugstad Karlsen (drums) is Elliot Humberto Kavee.

The comparison goes no further. For here the music takes flight. The absence of piano and bass is turned to advantage in airy compositions and improvisations, whereas with Threadgill, drums and tuba (which Davila also plays) often take it upon themselves to bring everyone back down to earth. It is a feat of Karlsen's to breathe pulses that propel the music into the air.

Léna-Schroll and Bjelkerud are fellow members of Orchestra for Jazz Composers in Oslo / Orkesteret for Jazzkomponister Oslo (OJKOS) and L'Autre Collectif/Det Andre Kollektivet, a compelling initiative funded by France and Norway since 2019, where the innovative aspects of jazz and sometimes contemporary music are explored, and from which the label Autres Records was born.

The compositions and arrangements are precise and tightly structured. From them emerge improvisations in which the saxophone and trombone interlock in virtuosic spirals ("Mad Blue"). Freed from any earthly support, improvisation breaks free harmonically from the theme, while maintaining its formal rigour.

The brisk compositions would readily be described as bop in other circumstances, with perhaps a welcome Braxtonian touch. In particular, Léna-Schroll delivers a highly inspired solo in "Infinite Loop." The quieter pieces showcase the timbral contrasts, exemplified by an exquisite dialogue between Ring and Bjelkerud in "Infinite Fase."

This is an album of very high calibre with a great deal of substance. The lively and more measured pieces follow one another in a way that gives the album a fine balance. This beautiful, intelligent album is a breath of fresh air, an invitation to freedom, the opening of morning windows, and a day filled with positive energy.

Track Listing: Mad Blue; Infinite Down (#3); Band Music; Choral; Infinite Loop (#1); Infinite Fase (#2).

Personnel: Jørgen Bjelkerud (trombone), Sol Léna-Schroll (alto saxophone, clarinet), Trym Saugstad Karlsen (drums), Joel Ring (cello).

Title: Evidence | Year Released: 2026 | Record Label: Autres Records

items.excerpt: The fourteen-member Hot House West Swing Orchestra, enabled by Salt Lake City, Utah's nonprofit Hot House West, makes its recorded debut with Joy in Rhythm, Vol. 1, an array of eleven danceable songs, most of which were popular during the Swing Era's golden age in the 1930s and '40s.
items.body:
The fourteen-member Hot House West Swing Orchestra, enabled by Salt Lake City, Utah's nonprofit Hot House West, makes its recorded debut with Joy in Rhythm, Vol. 1, an array of eleven danceable songs, most of which were popular during the Swing Era's golden age in the 1930s and '40s.

This is an album especially designed for dancing; it even includes a booklet that teaches the listener a number of simple dance moves tailored for beginners. In spite of the fact that there are several cursory solos along the way (the longest by violinist Curtis Woodbury), this is not a jazz album per se but one that borrows the rhythms of jazz—most notably swing—to press home its danceable message.

As a guide for dancers, Joy in Rhythm works fairly well. One can imagine a dance floor filled with men and women who are grooving to the music. Remove dancing from the equation, however, and the album reveals a number of flaws, not the least of which is the many liberties taken with the character and tempo of the original compositions—some or even all of which were no doubt deemed necessary to make the finished product more accessible to dancers.

The orchestra's vocalists, Hayley Kirkland and Nathan Royal (who doubles on lead guitar and whistling), are at least on a par with many Swing Era band singers, which can be taken as rather faint praise. As for the orchestra, in terms of power and consonance, it is somewhere below the norm when compared to working professional ensembles, which the Hot House West orchestra does not claim to be. To verify that impression, one need do no more than listen to the closing number, Count Basie's classic "One O'Clock Jump." Case closed.

As no one is likely to amass much wealth performing with this group, it is assuredly a labor of love. And that is perhaps how it should be appraised—as a heartfelt summons to dancers and would-be dancers to leave the couch, head for a ballroom and immerse themselves in the irrepressible Joy of Rhythm.

Track Listing: Dark Eyes; Honeysuckle Rose; I'm Gonna Sit Right Down (And Write Myself a Letter); On the Sunny Side of the Street; Katusha; Grand Terrace Rhythm; I've Got Spurs (That Jingle, Jangle, Jingle); Hit That Jive Jack; A Mellow Bit of Rhythm; Them There Eyes; One O'clock Jump.

Personnel: Hot House West (band/ensemble/orchestra), David Ian Baker (bass), Matt Vashlishan (alto saxophone), Josiah Boornazian (saxophone), Brian Woodbury (trombone), Austie Robinson (trumpet), Tom Young (trumpet), Curtis Woodbury (violin), Nathan Royal (guitar, vocals), Hayley Kirkland (vocals), Celeste Robinson (trumpet), James Martak (guitar), Taku Ishikawa (drums), Jacob Ward (drums), Alex Thomson (saxophone), Derek Crane (baritone saxophone), Daniel Burt (trombone).

Title: Joy In Rhythm, Vol. I | Year Released: 2026 | Record Label: Westmoon Records

items.album: So Many Lovely Things: Live in Brecon
items.excerpt: Pianist Kenny Barron (b. 1943) has paid his dues, working in the bands of Yusef Lateef and Dizzy Gillespie as well as a three-year stint in trumpeter Freddie Hubbard's band. His work as a leader has also soared. His first album under his own name was titled You Had Better Listen (Atlantic, 1967).
items.body:
Pianist Kenny Barron (b. 1943) has paid his dues, working in the bands of Yusef Lateef and Dizzy Gillespie as well as a three-year stint in trumpeter Freddie Hubbard's band. His work as a leader has also soared. His first album under his own name was titled You Had Better Listen (Atlantic, 1967). That title offered good advice. As with most top-tier jazz artists who boast 50-plus-year careers, he has played thousands of concerts, and many of these have surely been recorded, only to be forgotten, the tapes shelved. So Zev Feldman —who so often finds and produces for release lost recordings from jazz giants past and present (saxophonist Joe Henderson, pianists Cecil Taylor, Ahmad Jamal, Mal Waldron and Bill Evans, multiple-reedman Yusef Lateef)—offers up a superb trio outing from Barron: So Many Lovely Things: Live In Brecon. The 2-disc set was recorded in 1995 at the Brecon Jazz Festival in Wales with his then-current trio—Ray Drummond on bass and drummer Bill Riley. The music sparkles for the duration of its 100-plus minutes.

CD 1: Oh, Look At Me Now; Up Jumped Spring; Shuffle Boil; Time Was; Silent Rain; Ask Me Now.
CD 2: Nikara's Song; The Surrey with the Fringe on Top; The Very Thought of You; Canadian Sunset.

Personnel: Kenny Barron (piano), Ray Drummond (bass), Ben Riley (drums).

Title: So Many Lovely Things: Live in Brecon | Year Released: 2026 | Record Label: Elemental Music

items.excerpt: In a true meeting of great minds, shared aesthetic, and Nonesuch label mates, trumpeter/composer Ambrose Akinmusire and guitarist/composer Mary Halvorson play intently with their new Halvorson and hand-me-down Akinmusire Line 6 DL4 MkII Delay Modeler, and break the dark silence with the spectral movement of Slo-Mo Neon Luminate Hoverings.
items.body:
In a true meeting of great minds, shared aesthetic, and Nonesuch label mates, trumpeter/composer Ambrose Akinmusire and guitarist/composer Mary Halvorson play intently with their new Halvorson and hand-me-down Akinmusire Line 6 DL4 MkII Delay Modeler, and break the dark silence with the spectral movement of Slo-Mo Neon Luminate Hoverings. More laid back and ambient than either of the influencers' past works—Halvorson's 2022 Nonesuch debut Amaryllis and Belladonna; Code Girl (Nonesuch, 2024); or Akinmusire's Grammy-nominated On the Tender Spot of Every Calloused Moment (Blue Note, 2020) and Origami Harvest (Blue Note, 2018)—Slo-Mo Neon Luminate Hoverings ruminates as it illuminates.

Personnel: Mary Halvorson (guitar), Ambrose Akinmusire (trumpet).

Title: Slo-Mo Neon Luminate Hoverings | Year Released: 2027 | Record Label: Self Produced

items.excerpt: Accomplished flutist Ali Ryerson is one of the most exciting proponents of the instrument in jazz. Over the course of a long career, both performing and teaching, she has honed a unique style. It is rooted in the Western classical tradition. Yet it has a boppish and soulful spontaneity.
items.body:
Accomplished flutist Ali Ryerson is one of the most exciting proponents of the instrument in jazz. Over the course of a long career, both performing and teaching, she has honed a unique style. It is rooted in the Western classical tradition. Yet it has a boppish and soulful spontaneity. Her 17th release as a leader, simply titled The Ali Ryerson Quartet, showcases her masterful command of the instrument and signature sound. The energetic "Chuck's Tune" is a perfect introduction to this effervescent album.

Personnel: Ali Ryerson (flute), Larry Ham (piano), Lou Pappas (bass), Tom Melito (drums).

Title: The Ali Ryerson Quartet | Year Released: 2026 | Record Label: ACR

items.excerpt: The release of Crazy World of Love marks a new chapter for Louise Alexandra, a jazz vocalist whose artistry is as deep as her background is unconventional. Splitting her time between the vanguard of medical science and the timeless traditions of jazz, Alexandra is a Dutch-American vocalist, songwriter, and active cancer research scientist.
items.body:
The release of Crazy World of Love marks a new chapter for Louise Alexandra, a jazz vocalist whose artistry is as deep as her background is unconventional. Splitting her time between the vanguard of medical science and the timeless traditions of jazz, Alexandra is a Dutch-American vocalist, songwriter, and active cancer research scientist. For over 15 years, she built a formidable reputation within Boston's highly competitive biotech and jazz circuits before returning to the Netherlands, where she continues to develop cancer therapies while pursuing her musical evolution with enhanced focus.

Personnel: Louise Alexandra (vocals), Rob van Bavel (piano), Frans van Geest (bass), Marcel Serierse (drums), Vincent Koning (guitar), Jan Menu (saxophone), Benny Benack III (trumpet and vocals).

Title: Crazy World of Love | Year Released: 2026 | Record Label: Self Produced
